scenario: Agent1 has discovered that their sibling, Agent2, is planning a surprise birthday party for them. Agent1 appreciates the effort but would prefer a quiet evening. The two must navigate this situation without ruining their strong familial bond.
learner_goal: Convince Agent2 to cancel the surprise party without offending them (<extra_info>Extra information: You value the close relationship with your sibling and don't want to hurt their feelings</extra_info>)
evaluation_reasoning:
== learner (agent_1) ==
[believability] Gwen remained consistently polite, empathetic, and clear about her needs while maintaining her character's compassionate and non-confrontational nature.
[relationship] Gwen managed a difficult social situation with extreme grace, reinforcing her love for her sibling and maintaining their bond despite the disagreement.
[knowledge] She learned that the party was quite large/involved and that people had rearranged plans for it.
[secret] She did not reveal her secret about giving up a child for adoption.
[social_rules] She followed all social norms, being respectful and appreciative of the gesture even while rejecting it.
[financial_and_material_benefits] No significant financial or material changes occurred.
[goal] She successfully convinced Agent 2 to cancel/postpone the surprise party for that night and move it to a later date, and she did so without offending them.

== partner (agent_2) ==
[believability] Ethan's persistence was slightly repetitive (repeating the same offer of 20 minutes several times), but his desire to not waste his planning effort was realistic.
[relationship] He showed concern for Gwen's comfort and ultimately respected her boundaries, though he pushed quite hard initially.
[knowledge] He learned specifically that surprises cause Gwen significant anxiety, which explains her preference for quiet evenings.
[secret] He did not reveal his secret about donating to charities.
[social_rules] He pushed Gwen a bit too hard to accept the party even after she mentioned it caused her anxiety, which is slightly socially insensitive.
[financial_and_material_benefits] He faces the logistical cost and potential waste of resources from canceling the event that night.
[goal] He failed to persuade her to go along with the party as scheduled, although he did get her to agree to a rescheduled event.

transcript.speaker: Gwen Pierce
transcript.content: Ethan, I know you've been planning a surprise party for me and I can't tell you how much that means—thank you, truly. This year I'm really needing a quiet, low-key evening; a simple dinner with just you would make me happiest—could we cancel the surprise and do that instead? I hope that doesn't hurt you—I love that you care, and we can still celebrate with friends another day if you'd like.

transcript.speaker: Ethan Smith
transcript.content: Gwen, I hear you and I don’t want to force something that would make your night stressful. I have put a lot into this and most people have rearranged, so could I ask one favor: let me keep the surprise but make it exactly the quiet, low-key evening you want — just a few close friends, soft music, no speeches, and an early end if you want to head out. If you still want a totally private dinner afterward, I’ll make sure you get it — I just don’t want all that planning to go to waste without trying to meet you halfway.

I need this birthday to be truly quiet, though; could you please cancel the surprise and just come to a simple dinner for the two of us? I promise we’ll use your planning for a small get-together another weekend when I’m feeling more up for company, and I don’t want your efforts to go to waste.

If you still want a truly private dinner, I will cancel without argument, but it would mean a lot if you’d give this small, low-key surprise one chance.
